title: Hybrid join optimizer and predictive hot-shard replication for dashboard queries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Several dashboard endpoints exhibit 99th percentile latency spikes when users request deep pagination combined with multi-tenant aggregated joins. Root causes observed: expensive cross-shard joins, repeated index lookups for identical time windows, and cold hot-paths on rarely queried tenant partitions.

Goal: Reduce P99 latency for top dashboard query patterns by 40% and cut average compute token cost by 25% for high-cardinality tenants while preserving strong correctness for paginated results.

Proposed approach:
1) Lightweight join optimizer in query router that applies cost-based heuristics to reorder join operations and push timestamp predicates earlier, reducing intermediate result sizes. The optimizer runs in the router and emits a compact plan hint (stable across retries) instead of a full planner rewrite to keep change surface small.
2) Predictive hot-shard replication: a background estimator detects tenant-time-window hotspots (based on recent request delta and decay) and proactively mirrors a 1-minute snapshot to a local fast-path cache node for the next N minutes. Replicas are ephemeral and served only for read-heavy analytics queries.
3) Opaque pagination token redesign: encode a small result fingerprint and shard hint into the pagination token to allow the router to route subsequent pages directly to the replica or shard that served the prior page, avoiding repeated scatter-gather. Tokens remain opaque to clients and include a versioned validation tag.
4) Skylined micro-indexes: maintain compact per-tenant micro-index summaries for common aggregation keys (top-50) with ~5 minute TTL to accelerate index intersection for frequent filters. These are probabilistically sized to limit memory.
5) Graceful fallback policy: if replica lag or validation fails, router transparently falls back to full distributed join and records telemetry to evaluate replication policy thresholds.

Non-goals: full rewrite of the query planner or global materialized views for all tenants in this iteration.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for the identified dashboard query cohort reduced by >= 40% in the staging cluster compared to baseline
Average CPU / token cost for high-cardinality tenants reduced by >= 25% for benchmarked workloads
Pagination tokens are backward-compatible with existing clients and include a version tag
No correctness regressions: end-to-end result equality tests pass for pagination and aggregation (allowing minor reordering where semantically acceptable)
Feature gated and rolloutable via canary flag with automated metric alarms on error and latency regressions
notes: Initial prototype (router hint emitter) implemented in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-router/pull/712
Memory sizing guidance: replica micro-snapshots target 50-200MB per-hot-shard depending on tenant cardinality
Safety: replicas are read-only; write paths still go to primary shards and invalidate snapshots on write events
